earned_by: Disposable scoping on 2026-10-22, not evidence: 'x or (h != h')' gave 1.531, 1.551, 1.520 bits on square tori with both sides odd (sides 9, 17, 33) and 1.971, 2.018, 1.996 on 1:2 tori, against Pinson's 1.50846 and 1.98520. CONTACT-CENSUS-20261022-001A-P001 proves the ten classes, the regimes, the bipartite-percolation reduction and two-sided bounds; the conformal limit is a prediction.
question: On square-lattice tori with one placed three-variable contact on every edge, hidden joints and fair visible spokes: do the ten classes show their predicted regimes, and does the emergence of 'x or (h != h')' match Pinson's conformal prediction on several torus shapes and on rotated tori?

public_inputs.C1_census: class representatives with transfer pairs (spoke 0, spoke 1): vacuum classes (I,J), (U,L), (A1,I), (A1,J), (J,L), (A1,L) on 9 x 9, 17 x 17 and 9 x 18 tori, 2,000 samples; parity (I,S) on 3 x 3 (200,000 samples) and 3 x 5 (1,000,000); swap-or-order (S,L) on 3 x 3 and 5 x 5 (200,000); not-all-equal (A1,A2) and 'x or (h != h')' (S,J) on a x a tori, a in {9, 17, 33, 65}, 8,000 samples
public_inputs.C3_contrast: not-all-equal on 17 x 34 and 33 x 66, 8,000 samples
public_inputs.C4_placements: all 12 placements of not-all-equal and all 12 of 'x or (h != h')' on the 17 x 17 torus, 4,000 samples each
public_inputs.controls: not-all-equal and 'x or (h != h')' on the bipartite 16 x 16 and 32 x 32 tori, 2,000 samples each

definitions: Tori have a rows and b columns; edges are oriented east and north. A sample draws one fair spoke per edge; it is consistent when some joint assignment satisfies every edge's transfer. E = -log2 of the consistent fraction with a delta-method standard error; zero consistent samples give the lower bound log2(N). 'x or (h != h')' is judged by two independent tests: limited backtracking on the transfer tables, and union-find bipartiteness of the edges whose spoke selects disequality (both on every sample up to side 33, the first 1,000 samples beyond).

predictions.H_conformal: for each of the five rectangular shapes, the weighted mean E over its two largest sizes lies within 3 standard errors plus 0.01 bits of the Pinson limit; the rotated squares' weighted mean lies within 3 standard errors plus 0.01 of 1.508460
predictions.H_census: vacuum classes are consistent in every sample; parity has E within 3 standard errors of 10 on 3 x 3 and of 16 on 3 x 5; swap-or-order has E(5 x 5) > E(3 x 3) + 3; the two critical classes have |slope| <= 0.05 bits per doubling over sides 9-65, and their family means differ by more than 0.5 bits
predictions.H_placements: within each critical class, every placement's E on 17 x 17 lies within 3.5 standard errors of the class's weighted mean
predictions.controls: the two critical classes are consistent in every sample on bipartite tori; the two tests agree on every doubly judged sample

decision_rule: If a control fails, the run is invalid. Supported when H_conformal, H_census and H_placements all hold; refuted when some rectangular shape's mean deviates from its Pinson limit by more than 5 standard errors plus 0.02 bits; closed null otherwise.
stop_rule: Stop immediately if a control fails; otherwise stop after the frozen roster.
red_team_r0: Identifiability: the reduction (proved) makes the 'x or (h != h')' observable exactly a percolation topology event; the test compares it with an independently derived formula.
Leakage: Pinson's values enter only as frozen hypotheses; the producer never reads them.
Solver error: two independent consistency tests judge the critical contact.
Finite size: the allowance of 0.01 bits covers corrections at sides 33-65; a failure beyond 5 standard errors plus 0.02 refutes.
Multiplicity: six shape comparisons (five rectangular, one rotated) with a fixed rule.
nonclaims: Monte Carlo estimates on finite tori; agreement with Pinson's formula supports, and does not prove, the conformal limit.
Lattices and placements are declared; nothing is said about space.
Only one contact per torus, uniformly oriented.
forbidden_inputs: Pinson's predicted values or scoping values as producer inputs
